title: Metabolic Glycoengineering of Sialic Acid Using N-acyl-modified Mannosamines
protocol: Dissolve 8.1 mg sodium methoxide in 50 mL methanol (3 mM) in a 100 mL glass bottle with a stir bar.
Store the sodium methoxide solution at room temperature for several weeks.
Combine 8.766 g NaCl, 157 mg Tris-HCl, and 146 mg EDTA in a 100 mL glass bottle with a stir bar and dissolve in 80 mL water.
Adjust the pH of the stirring solution to 8.0 using sodium hydroxide (1 M) or HCl (20%).
Add water to achieve a final volume of 100 mL for the Tris-HCl buffer.
Filter the Tris-HCl buffer through a 0.22 µm sterile filter system.
Store the Tris-HCl buffer at 4 °C for several weeks.
Dissolve 10 mg aprotinin in 1 mL water (1.54 mM).
Aliquot the aprotinin solution into 10 x 1.5 mL-plastic tubes (100 µL each).
Store the aprotinin aliquots at -20 °C for several weeks.
Dissolve 10 mg leupeptin in 2 mL water (10 mM).
Aliquot the leupeptin solution into 10 x 1.5 mL-plastic tubes.
Store the leupeptin aliquots at -20 °C for several weeks.
Dissolve 34.8 mg PMSF in 2 mL ethanol (100 mM).
Aliquot the PMSF solution into 10 x 1.5 mL-plastic tubes.
Store the PMSF aliquots at -20 °C for several weeks.
Combine 15.62 mg DMB with 352 µL β-mercaptoethanol.
Add 48 µL sodium bisulfite solution to the mixture.
Dissolve in 9.6 mL water to achieve a 6.9 mM DMB, 500 mM β-mercaptoethanol, and 0.19% sodium bisulfite solution.
Aliquot 250 μL of the DMB solution into 40 x 1.5 mL plastic tubes.
Store aliquoted DMB solution protected from light at -20°C for several weeks.
Add 770.3 µL of 100% TFA to 9.23 mL water in a 15 mL plastic tube.
Store the resulting 1 M trifluoroacetic acid (TFA) solution at 4°C for several weeks.
Mix 92.4 µL of TFA with 9.91 mL water in a 15 mL plastic tube to create a 120 mM TFA solution.
Store the prepared 120 mM TFA solution at 4°C for several weeks.
Dissolve 160 mg NaOH in 10 mL water in a 15 mL plastic tube to prepare a 400 mM sodium hydroxide (NaOH) solution.
Store the resulting 400 mM NaOH solution at 4°C for several weeks.
Dissolve 5.84 g NaCl, 0.1 g Tris(hydroxymethyl)aminomethan (Tris), 0.1 g CaCl2, and 0.95 g MgCl2 in 100 mL water to prepare Western blot lysis buffer.
Adjust the pH of the lysis buffer solution to 7.8.
Add 100 µL each of protease inhibitors (aprotinin, leupeptin, PMSF) before using the prepared lysis buffer.
Dissolve 0.3 g Tris, 1.5 g glycine, and 0.1 g SDS in 100 mL water to prepare sodium dodecyl sulfate polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis (SDS-PAGE) buffer.
Adjust the pH of the SDS-PAGE buffer solution to 7.3.
Dissolve 0.3 g Tris and 1.1 g glycine in 90 mL water to prepare Western blot buffer.
Add 10 mL ethanol to complete the preparation of the Western blot buffer.
Store both prepared buffers at room temperature (RT).
Dissolve 1 g of fat-free milk powder in 25 mL phosphate-buffered saline (PBS).
Always prepare fresh blocking solution.
Dissolve 431.2 mg mannosamine hydrochloride in 10 mL 3 mM sodium methoxide solution.
Cool the mixture to 0 °C on ice.
Slowly add dropwise 210 µL propionyl chloride to the stirring solution for ManNProp synthesis.
Incubate the stirring mixture at 0 °C for 4 hours.
Transfer the solution into a 50 mL plastic tube with holes poked in the lid.
Rapidly freeze the solution using liquid nitrogen and lyophilize it for 48 hours or until completely dried.
Mix 350 g silica gel 60 with 750 mL ethyl-acetate/methanol/water (15:2:1).
Fill a glass column with the silica gel 60 suspension and wash with an additional 100 mL ethyl-acetate/methanol/water before use.
Dissolve 5 g dried product from step 2.3 in 10 mL ethyl-acetate/methanol/water (15:2:1).
Load the dissolved products onto the silica gel column using a pipette.
Collect 4 mL fractions after 500 mL elution volume for ManNProp.
Transfer eluted fractions into 15 mL plastic tubes.
Poke 3 - 6 holes into the lid of the tube with a thin needle.
Rapidly freeze the solution using liquid nitrogen.
Lyophilize the frozen solution until completely dried.
Culture Kelly neuroblastoma cells in RPMI medium containing 10% fetal bovine serum, 100 U penicillin, 100 mg streptomycin, and 2 mM L-glutamine supplemented with 5 mM ManNAc, ManNProp, or ManNBut.
Incubate cells at 37 °C in a 5% CO2 atmosphere.
Replace medium every 24 hours.
Detach Kelly neuroblastoma cells by incubating them for 10 min with trypsin/EDTA solution.
Count detached cells using a Neubauer chamber or cell counter.
Seed 1 x 10^5 cells in 500 µL of medium into a 48-well tissue culture plate to measure sialic acid monosaccharides.
Seed 1 x 10^6 cells in 3 mL of medium onto a 6 cm diameter cell culture dish for polysialic acids analysis.
Treat cells for 5 - 7 days for high metabolic efficiency.
Decant the medium after treatment.
Wash plates/dishes with PBS.
Incubate cells for 10 min with trypsin/EDTA (0.25%, 0.02% in PBS).
Neutralize trypsin by adding cell culture medium to detached cells.
Transfer detached cells into 15 mL plastic tubes.
Centrifuge samples for 3 min at 500 x g and discard supernatant.
Add 5 mL PBS and centrifuge cells (see step 3.3).
Repeat washing procedure two more times.
Combine 5 mL Tris-HCl buffer, 5 μL aprotinin solution, 20 μL leupeptin solution, and 50 μL PMSF solution to prepare HPLC lysis buffer.
Re-suspend collected cell pellets in 500 μl ice-cold HPLC lysis-buffer.
Ultra-sonicate samples with an ultra-sonic processor needle three times for a period of 30 s at medium-high amplitudes.
Cool samples on ice for at least 1 min between cycles.
Centrifuge the lysed cell samples for 2 h at 20,000 x g and 4 °C.
Separate the supernatant (approximately 480 µL) in 1.5 mL plastic tubes.
Determine the protein concentration of these fractions using a suitable assay such as Bradford or BCA.
Add 150 µL 1 M TFA-solution to the separated membrane fractions.
Incubate the samples for 4 h at 80 °C with shaking at 200 - 600 rpm.
Centrifuge the samples for approximately 30 min at 20,000 x g and 21 °C using 0.5 mL filter tubes with 3 kDa exclusion membranes until the upper phase volume is less than 20 µL.
Transfer the lower phase containing smaller molecules into 2 mL plastic tubes.
Poke 2 - 4 holes into the caps of the plastic tubes with a thin needle.
Rapid freeze the samples using liquid nitrogen and then lyophilize them overnight.
Re-suspend the dried samples in 10 µL 120 mM TFA solution.
Add 50 µL DMB solution to the re-suspended samples.
Transfer samples into dark 1.5 mL tubes.
For standards, dissolve 1 µL Neu5Ac (60 ng/mL) or 1 µL Neu5Gc (60 ng/mL) in 10 µL 120 mM TFA solution in dark 1.5 mL tubes.
Add 50 µL DMB solution to the standards.
Incubate the cell membrane samples and the standards for 1.5 h at 56 °C protected from light.
After incubation, add 4 µL 400 mM NaOH solution to each sample to stop the labeling reaction.
Degas all solvents prior to measurements if the HPLC system lacks an internal degasser.
Set the temperature of the column to 40 °C.
Configure the fluorescence detector with 373 nm for excitation and 448 nm for emission.
Inject 10 μL sample volume.
Separate the probes for 50 min at 0.5 mL/min flow rate using methanol/acetonitrile/water (6:8:86) as the eluent.
Collect peaks of interest for mass spectrometry analysis.
Wash the column for 7.5 min at 1.0 mL/min flow rate with methanol/acetonitrile/water (6:25:69).
Re-equilibrate the system for 7.5 min at 1.0 mL/min flow rate using methanol/acetonitrile/water (6:8:86).
Inject 20 µL of collected sample into an LC/Mass Selective Detector system.
Use 79.9% methanol, 20% isopropyl alcohol, and 0.1% formic acid as eluent with a flow rate of 0.5 mL/min.
Set the capillary voltage to 4 kV and capillary temperature to 350 °C.
Select the peak of interest in the total ion chromatogram using the evaluation software.
View the mass spectrum of the resolved peak.
Display the positive mass/charge ratio between 300 and 700.
Add 1 mL Western blot lysis buffer to cell pellets.
Vortex the mixture thoroughly.
Incubate for 30 min on ice, vortexing every 5 min.
Centrifuge the samples for 1.5 h at 20,000 x g and 4 °C.
Collect the supernatant containing proteins from the lysed cells.
Determine the protein concentration of the protein fractions using the Bradford or BCA assay.
Dilute the samples to a protein concentration of 1.5 µg/µL in lysis buffer.
Add 10 µL Laemmli sample buffer to 90 µL protein fraction (1.5 µg/µL).
Boil the sample for 5 min.
Use 8% SDS-acrylamide gels with 20 - 30 µL pockets and 0.75 or 1 mm thickness.
Run the gel at 25 mA for 2 h at RT.
Remove the glass cover from the gel.
Cut out and discard the upper part of the gel containing the loading pockets.
Place the gel on a nitrocellulose membrane (0.2 µm), previously soaked in Western blot buffer.
Transfer the proteins to nitrocellulose according to the recommendation of the system (e.g., 250 mA for 1 h at 4 °C).
Remove the nitrocellulose membrane from the blotting system.
Stain the blot with Ponceau red to visualize the proteins.
Transfer the nitrocellulose membrane into a plastic chamber and add 10 mL blocking solution.
Incubate for 1 h at RT or overnight at 4 °C.
Decant the blocking solution.
Add monoclonal anti-polySia 735 antibody (1 µg/mL) in PBS.
Incubate the membrane for 1 h at RT or overnight at 4 °C.
Wash the membrane at least three times for 5 min with PBS.
Mix polyclonal anti-mouse IgG secondary antibody (1 µg/mL) coupled to horseradish peroxidase (HRP) or a fluorescent label in PBS.
Incubate the membrane for 1 h at room temperature.
Wash the membrane at least three times for 5 min with PBS.
Transfer the membrane onto a plate of an appropriate imager.
Detect the signal according to the manufacturer's instructions.
